descriptionChirho: The physical head of a person, animal, or statue image, used literally across all pronominal suffixes and with prepositional prefix
Metaphorical extension of 'head' to denote a chief or leader among a group, as evidenced by Hindi 'मुखिया' (chief) and Swahili 'viongozi' (leaders)
Abstract sense meaning the sum, summary, or main point of a matter, as in Daniel 7:1 'the sum of the matters', supported by multilingual glosses 'resumen' (Spa), 'muhtasari' (Swa), 'मुख्य' (Hin)
